Subject: Speedproof: post-call recap + immediate asks

Quick recap from the call with Carolyn / QuantaSys (joined w/ their infra lead and an SRE):

- They want a side-by-side verification vs the hyperscaler-managed endpoint they currently use. Primary asks: p95/p99 tail-latency, tokens/sec (seq len distributions), and cost-per-token estimate under our Dedicated config.
- They are particularly sensitive to p99 on long-context requests (2k–8k tokens) and burst behaviour (microbursts).
- Competitive claims to validate: their current vendor says they get consistent p99 ~2200ms at 2k context, and tokens/sec ~1200 on their provisioned cluster.

Attachments: call recording + our benchmark-probe-template.csv (filled skeleton). Carolyn also promised a compressed sample of their baseline logs (attached in follow-up).

My asks (short-term):
1) Can engineering scope a two-phase A/B run we can offer QuantaSys next week? Phase A = synthetic canonical traces (our infra), Phase B = their real sampled traces replayed in our harness.
2) Define two model / config variants to compare: (a) Redwood-default quantized profile (INT8/8-bit ASE) and (b) Redwood-latency-optimized (FP16, aggressive kernel selection, smaller batching). Capture p95/p99, p50, tokens/sec, and CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Concrete test matrix (seq length buckets: 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192), targets = p95 and p99, and token-rate per second.

Notes: sales ask is a short customer-friendly summary they can share with procurement. They want an outline of the lab plan + ballpark delta vs hyperscaler within 48 hours.

Next step: Marissa, Ben — can you draft the two-config test matrix and estimated runtime (hours + cost) by EOD tomorrow? I'll send a brief one-pager to Carolyn with the timeline.

Thanks,
Jonas

--

On Mon, Jul 22, 2029 at 14:05, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:

+1 on the two-phase approach. My suggested concrete plan below (high level):

Phase A — synthetic canonical sweep (3–4 hours):
- Workload: generated traces that match QuantaSys token/seq distribution they provided in the probe template.
- Variants:
  * V1 (cost-first): INT8 quantized profile, batching target 64, KV-cache warm start disabled
  * V2 (latency-first): FP16 kernels, batching target 8, aggressive kernel preselection, KV-cache warm start enabled
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies (server-side), tokens/sec (aggregate and per-instance), GPU occupancy, and tail queuing. Produce plots (latency CDF) and a short narrative.

Phase B — customer trace replay (4–6 hours):
- Replays: 10k requests sampled from provided logs across seq buckets. Run V1 and V2 back-to-back on the same Dedicated hardware profile. Capture cost extrapolation for each (tokens x time).

Measurement details:
- Use 99th percentile over 1-minute windows for p99 reporting to avoid single-outlier spikes.
- Report tokens/sec as both instantaneous and 1-min average.

Operational asks for Ben:
- Confirm Dedicated pool size and instance types we can reserve for the runs (ideally 2x of the target profile to avoid queuing noise).
- Provide rough hours & infra estimate so Jonas can give a procurement-friendly number.

Deliverables: short readout doc + 1-slide delta summary we can share in <48h.

I'll draft the readout template tonight and attach it.

Marissa
